subject: sociology

moments.title: Family and Kinship in East London
moments.body: Their Bethnal Green study documents dense extended kinship networks in a working-class East End community.
moments.takeaway: Empirical sociology challenged assumptions about family decline.

moments.title: The Symmetrical Family
moments.body: Young and Willmott argue post-war affluence is producing more symmetrical conjugal relationships across classes.
moments.takeaway: Family forms shift with economic conditions.

moments.title: The Sociology of Housework
moments.body: Oakley's interviews with 40 London housewives find domestic labour experienced as monotonous and isolating, despite affluence.
moments.takeaway: Feminist critique punctured the symmetrical-family thesis.

now.title: Family sociology today
now.body: Contemporary research addresses cohabitation, same-sex families, transnational families and care chains.
now.open_questions: What counts as a household when housing costs force adult children to remain at home?

reflection: Young and Willmott's institute (the Institute of Community Studies) shaped UK family sociology for decades.
